messages:
kevin: Heads-up — we have a Priority 1 from Acme. They upgraded to our new Python client and immediately saw 401s and a billing spike from retries. Ticket: https://acme.support/12345

maria: ugh. do we know what changed in the client? customer says the token is set but server rejects it. they pasted a curl that works, client doesn't.

kevin: their curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood/prod/chain` succeeds. python client sends header `X-API-Key: token` (old name) — server changed to only accept Authorization in openapi. Looks like generated client mapped the security scheme name differently after regen.

alex: I dug in quickly — OpenAPI `components.securitySchemes` had the scheme key renamed from `Authorization` -> `apiKeyAuth` in a recent spec change. Our generator uses the key name as the header name in some SDKs (ugh). The spec diff in CI: `- components.securitySchemes.Authorization` -> `+ components.securitySchemes.apiKeyAuth`.

sasha: That explains 401s. Why billing spike?

maria: SDK has automatic retry on 5xx and 429. But because the auth header is wrong, server returns 401 then our client treats 401 as retriable (bug) and retries, each retry counted toward usage (embedding calls inside loop). Customer ran a batch job and hit ~30x tokens.

kevin: repro steps from customer (condensed):
```
pip install redwood-sdk==2.1.0
python -c "from redwood import Client; c=Client(); c.generate('hi')"
```
Server logs show `missing auth header` then repeated requests with same id.

alex: Minimal fix options:
- revert generator change (map spec key -> Authorization header name) and regen all SDKs
- add compatibility on server to accept old header names for a grace period
- patch SDKs to always set `Authorization` when an apiKey security exists (regardless of key name)

jen-ci: CI note: regen job passed because client generation step uses the updated OpenAPI but we don't run an end-to-end acceptance test that makes an authenticated call. Our CI only runs unit client build + lint. So drift slipped through.

maria: Recommended immediate remediation: 1) add server shim to accept `X-API-Key` for the next 48 hours, 2) hotfix Python client to treat 401 as non-retriable for auth failures (or inspect header missing) and release patch, 3) open PR to regen TS/Go with compatibility patch.

alex: I'll open a PR to change generator mapping and bump python/ts/go packages. Also adding an integration test that does a real auth request post-regen.

sasha: For long term: CI should fail regen if security scheme rename occurs without a changelog entry and we should require a smoke auth call in regen pipeline. I'll draft a ticket.

support-bot: Created support escalation incident: INC-2026. Linked to PRs and customer ticket.

maria: I'll reply to the customer with a workaround (set header manually in their client: `client._transport.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'`) and ETA for patch. :+1:

kevin: thanks all — prioritizing this for today. keep updates here and ping @oncall if we need to coordinate dedicated infra changes.
